item_text: There are n lamps L_0, . . . , L_(n-1) in a circle (n > 1), where we denote L_(n+k) = L_k. (A lamp at all times is either on or off.) Perform steps s_0, s_1, . . . as follows: at step s_i, if L_(i-1) is lit, switch L_i from on to off or vice versa, otherwise do nothing. Initially all lamps are on. Show that: (a) There is a positive integer M(n) such that after M(n) steps all the lamps are on again; (b) If n = 2^k, we can take M(n) = n^2 - 1; (c) If n = 2^k + 1, we can take M(n) = n^2 - n + 1.
